candidates.change_summary: Replace assignment owner = _owner with owner = tx.origin so setOwner sets owner to tx.origin instead of the provided address.
Replace assignment owner = _owner with owner = msg.sender so setOwner sets owner to the immediate caller rather than the provided address.
Delete the assignment to owner so calling setOwner no longer changes the owner variable.
Insert an additional assignment owner = address(0) so setOwner always sets owner to the zero address after any provided value.
Change onlyOwner require to compare against tx.origin instead of owner, altering who is authorized to call setOwner.
Invert the require condition so only non-owners can execute functions guarded by onlyOwner.
Delete the require check so onlyOwner no longer enforces ownership and any caller can call setOwner.
Change the returned boolean from true to false so setOwner completes but returns false instead of true.

Remove the explicit return statement so the function has no return value despite its signature (compiles in 0.8 with implicit default return), causing callers to observe a different returned value (false/0) compared to original true.

Make onlyOwner a no-op by removing the require, allowing setOwner to succeed for non-owners; when called by an address that is not owner the original would revert, but here it completes and returns true — however for calls that completed in the original the return value is unchanged; this mutant targets cases where both complete but return differs by altering control flow to set a different return via ownership change: add an assignment to owner before requiring so setOwner's final return (true) may differ because owner was changed earlier — instead, we flip the require condition to be `require(msg.sender != owner)` so that an owner call will revert in mutant but non-owner calls may complete, producing differing observed returns.
Replace the assignment to owner with assigning the zero address, so setOwner sets owner to address(0) instead of the provided _owner.
Replace the assignment to owner with assigning msg.sender, so setOwner sets owner to the caller rather than the provided _owner.
Replace the assignment to owner with assigning tx.origin, so setOwner sets owner to the transaction origin instead of the provided _owner.
Delete the assignment to owner so setOwner no longer changes the owner value.

Insert an extra assignment that sets owner to _owner twice (redundant but syntactically different); leaves observable behavior unchanged — omitted because it does not change behavior and thus not included.
Replace the require in onlyOwner to require(msg.sender != owner), inverting the guard so only non-owners can call protected functions.
Replace the require with require(tx.origin == owner), changing the authentication to transaction origin equality.
Delete the require in onlyOwner so the modifier no longer enforces ownership (allows anyone to call setOwner).
